youtube.title: Inter's greatest striker ever: Meazza or Ronaldo? #Shorts
youtube.description:
Inter's greatest striker ever — Meazza or Ronaldo? We picked Meazza. Your turn.
The Italian Inter press in English every morning, free: https://www.nerazzurridaily.com/go/yt/?v=debate2

THE DEBATE — a weekly fan-made argument, not the news.
Giuseppe Meazza (1927–40, 1946–47): 284 goals in 408 Inter games, the club record; Serie A top scorer in 1930, 1936 and 1938; the stadium has carried his name since 1980.
Ronaldo (1997–2002): 59 goals in 99 Inter games; Ballon d'Or 1997 and 2002; scored in the 1998 UEFA Cup final win over Lazio.
Christian Vieri (1999–2005): 123 goals in 190 games; Serie A top scorer 2002–03.
Diego Milito (2009–14): 75 goals in 171 games; both goals in the 2010 Champions League final.
Mauro Icardi (2013–19): 124 goals in 219 games; Serie A top scorer 2014–15 and 2017–18.
Lautaro Martínez (2018–): 179 goals in 381 games through Sept. 19, 2026, third on Inter's all-time list.
For the record: the Ballon d'Or was first awarded in 1956, after Meazza's career. Second on the all-time list is Alessandro Altobelli with 209.
Sources: inter.it (Hall of Fame, player archive, all-time scorers list), RSSSF, uefa.com, Wikipedia.
Fan-made — not affiliated with FC Internazionale Milano.
#Inter #ForzaInter #SerieA #Meazza #Ronaldo #Shorts
youtube.comment: Meazza, Ronaldo — or someone we left off (Altobelli? Boninsegna? Ibrahimović?). Name your pick. Reply in the comments. https://www.nerazzurridaily.com/go/yt/?v=debate2-pinned

sources.claim: Meazza: 284 goals in 408 Inter appearances, 'the greatest goalscorer in the club's history'; 14 seasons; captain for nine years
Meazza totals by competition (league 365/243, European 27/29, cups 16/12 = 408/284); Scudetti 1929-30, 1937-38, 1939-40; Coppa Italia 1938-39

Inter all-time scorers (article dated Sept 19, 2026): Meazza 284 (408), Altobelli 209 (466), Lautaro Martínez 179 (381), Boninsegna 171, Mazzola 161, Cevenini 158, Lorenzi 143, Nyers 133, Icardi 124 (219), Vieri 123 (190) — so Meazza is 75 clear of second place

Serie A top scorers: Meazza 1929-30 (31), 1935-36 (25), 1937-38 (20); 1997-98 Bierhoff 27 and 1998-99 Amoroso 22 (Ronaldo never won it); Vieri 2002-03 (24); Icardi 2014-15 (22) and 2017-18 (29); Lautaro 2023-24 (24), 2025-26 (17)
San Siro named Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on March 3, 1980; Inter spells 1927-1940 and 1946-47; Mitropa Cup runner-up 1933 (no European trophy); one match in 1939-40 through injury
Ronaldo: 99 caps, 59 goals, 1 trophy (UEFA Cup) — Inter Hall of Fame
Ronaldo: '99 appearances, 59 goals, one UEFA Cup, two Ballon d'Ors'; lifted the Ballon d'Or at San Siro on Jan. 4, 1998; scored Inter's third goal in the final against Lazio
1997 Ballon d'Or: Ronaldo (Barcelona / Internazionale), 222 points, presented Dec. 23, 1997
2002 Ballon d'Or: Ronaldo (Internazionale / Real Madrid), presented Dec. 12, 2002
Ballon d'Or first awarded in 1956 (Stanley Matthews); list shows Ronaldo 1997 (Inter Milan) and 2002 (Real Madrid) — two career wins
1998 UEFA Cup final: Lazio 0-3 Inter, Parc des Princes, Paris (Zamorano 5, Zanetti 60, Ronaldo 70)
1998 UEFA Cup final played May 6, 1998; scorers Zamorano 4', Zanetti 60', Ronaldo 70'
Vieri: six seasons, 190 appearances, 123 goals; 2002-03 Serie A top scorer; 2004-05 Coppa Italia

Milito: 171 caps, 75 goals, 6 trophies; 30 goals in his first season; decided the Scudetto at Siena, the Coppa Italia final v Roma, and scored a brace v Bayern Munich in the Champions League final in Madrid
Lautaro Martínez: 381 appearances, 179 goals; 3 Serie A, 3 Coppa Italia, 3 Super Cups
it.wikipedia club players page: Meazza 284 all-time record; Ronaldo 'vincitore in nerazzurro di due Palloni d'oro (1997 e 2002)'; Vieri 24 goals in 23 games in 2002-03
en.wikipedia records table (as of May 13, 2026) lists Meazza at 287 — see verification

verification: Meazza goals: inter.it says 284 in 408 (Hall of Fame, player archive, all-time list); en.wikipedia's records table shows 287 (246 league). inter.it used; 287 appears nowhere.

Meazza Scudetti are DISPUTED and therefore not on any frame: inter.it Hall of Fame prose says 'two Scudetti and one Coppa Italia', while its own stats box says 'Trophies 4' and the inter.it player archive and Wikipedia list three (1929-30, 1937-38, 1939-40 — he played one match in 1939-40). No Scudetto or trophy count for Meazza is shown or spoken.

Ronaldo's Ballons d'Or 'as an Inter player' are DISPUTED (inter.it and it.wikipedia credit both 1997 and 2002 to his Inter years; en.wikipedia lists the 2002 award under Real Madrid, presented Dec. 12, 2002). On screen: the chip 'Ballon d'Or 1997' and a versus row labelled 'Ballons d'Or (career)' = 2, which every source agrees on. The Ballon d'Or did not exist until 1956; said in the YouTube description.
'European trophies' Meazza 0: UEFA competitions began after his career; the Mitropa Cup existed and Inter were runners-up in 1933, so 0 is accurate.
1998 UEFA Cup final: Zamorano's goal is 4' on inter.it and 5' on uefa.com — not used on screen.
Era '1927–47' on frames is first-to-last season; he was away 1940-46 (description says 1927–40, 1946–47; the chip says 14 seasons per inter.it).
Lautaro's totals move weekly: 179 in 381 is inter.it's figure dated Sept. 19, 2026, used only in the YouTube description with that date.
Voice: 'Milito' added to nd_voice.py FIX (Italian G2P stressed the first syllable). '[Inter]'s' avoided — the tool voices the possessive as the letter S ('Inter ess'); last week's hook used it.
